analysis.title: "Why Does This Stock Never Work?": Everything You Need To Know Ahead Of Amazon Earnings
key_insights: Amazon (AMZN) reports Q3 after the close on Oct 29, 2026. The stock is up 4% from the July 30 close, in line with the Nasdaq 100 and behind Microsoft and Meta (both +16-17%). It jumped 15% the day after the Q2 report in July and gave most of it back.

UBS rates sentiment 9 out of 10 with hedge funds long and long-onlys overweight. Goldman's TMT desk has positioning at 8/10. JPMorgan's Schilsky rates investor expectations 7 out of 10, versus 5 for Alphabet.
JPMorgan's Schilsky argues the stock does not work partly because Street 2027 AWS estimates are too low. Investors who buy expected KPI revisions already treat a beat-and-raise as consensus.
Buyside bogey for AWS revenue growth is +42% y/y, per JPMorgan, UBS and Deutsche Bank. Goldman's desk had consensus at about 41% on Tuesday. Schilsky wrote when the Street was at +37%.
Consensus AWS margin is about 37% (Goldman), and Deutsche models 37.1%. Low-40s margin would be a beat of several points.
Q3 operating income guidance was $22.5-26.5B and the Street is at $26B. Buyside bogey is $28B.
Q4 guide expectations: revenue guidance $239-246B (Street $244.5B) and operating income $30-35B.
Street 2027 capex is a touch over $280B per JPMorgan, while buyside range is $320-375B, with the majority at $330-350B. 2026 capex plan is about $220B.
Goldman's mid-day color: Mag7 risk-reward into earnings has been challenging. MSFT beat and is down 150bps, misses are being punished, and the group may act as a source of funds.

Nasdaq 100 was down 170bps midday, Goldman's Hyperscaler basket down 330bps, S&P ex-AI up 115bps. Alphabet had its biggest drop on record after a Search miss, and Amazon was down almost 4% in sympathy.
Goldman's US sales trading prefers capped upside structures out to Dec, with the stock over 12% off its August highs. The derivatives desk likes AMZN 18Dec'26 call spreads.
Goldman's Coppersmith has the implied earnings move at 7.5% versus a 24-quarter average realized move of 6.6%, the richest of the three hyperscalers. The July move was about twice that average.
Deutsche models retail growth decelerating to 6% in Q3 from 16% in Q2. Amazon app DAUs ended the quarter down about 2% y/y, and Prime Day moved into June, creating a weak July comparison.

Agentic commerce is a key debate. Amazon blocked Meta's Muse agent from shopping on Amazon.com while Walmart signed with Meta. Deutsche says Sponsored Products slowed about 100bps in 3Q after about 300bps in 2Q.
Goldman's Sheridan (Buy, $375 PT) and UBS both view agentic risk as overstated near term. UBS calls it a pressure point for long-onlys.

Deutsche channel checks: NTM committed dollar growth rose from 35% in June to nearly 38% in September, consumption growth from 38% to 40%. AWS 2026 capacity is sold out and most large 2027 blocks are booked, per Jassy.
Business Insider reported Nvidia GB300 racks sitting idle in Amazon warehouses awaiting power. Amazon walked away from Loudoun County data center projects. Goldman lists idle racks as a watch item.

Funding is the central debate. Trailing twelve-month FCF was an outflow of $7.6B in Q2. Amazon sold £4.25B of sterling bonds and tried an $8B Nvidia chip SPV sale-leaseback. Hyperscaler off-balance-sheet obligations were $3.6T per the author's tally.

JPMorgan estimates AI infrastructure has absorbed over $500B of debt year-to-date, with hyperscaler funding costs up about 120bps. JPM credit analyst Spear says debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Microsoft launched a $25B-plus bond deal, its first in nine years.
Goldman's Privorotsky says the market is transitioning from rewarding capex growth to demanding evidence of returns.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Sheridan rates Buy with a $375 PT and says near-term AI risk looks overstated, with AI-referred traffic small but fast-growing and Amazon keeping engagement in its own ecosystem.
Goldman's derivatives desk likes AMZN 18Dec'26 call spreads and sales trading sees upside stand out with the stock over 12% off its August highs.
Alphabet had its biggest one-day drop on record after a Search miss revived AI share-loss fears, despite Google Cloud growth of +103%.
Microsoft beat on Azure (+48%) but traded down about 150bps and launched a $25B-plus bond deal, its first in nine years.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman calls it a digestion day in Tech, with large-cap drawdowns of 10-15% in GOOG, NOW and FTNT, and Mag7 possibly a source of funds.

earnings_insights: AMZN Q3 2026 preview, not yet reported as of the note: AWS revenue growth bogey +42% y/y buyside vs about 41% consensus (Goldman desk, Tuesday). Q2 AWS was +37% ex-FX.
AMZN Q3 2026 operating income: company guidance $22.5-26.5B, Street estimate $26B, buyside bogey $28B (JPM).
AMZN Q3 2026 revenue: Street estimate $202-203B versus company guidance $197-202B, with North America growth of about 6% and international about 8% ex-FX.
AMZN AWS margin estimate: consensus about 37% (Goldman), Deutsche models 37.1%.
AMZN Q4 2026 guide expectations: revenue guidance of $239-246B (Street $244.5B), operating income $30-35B.
AMZN full-year 2026 per Bloomberg consensus: revenue $829B, AWS $171.2B (+36% constant currency), advertising $83.8B (+22%).
Already reported: MSFT Azure +48% and Google Cloud +103%, with Alphabet's Search missing. Microsoft beat and fell about 150bps.
Deutsche models AMZN retail growth at 6% in Q3 versus 16% in Q2. Census non-store sales point to a slowdown.

trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman's derivatives desk likes Mag7 upside, specifically AMZN call spreads, with max loss limited to premium paid.
trade_ideas.risk: Max loss equals the premium paid.

Idle Nvidia GB300 racks waiting for power and data center project cancellations.
Rising debt and off-balance-sheet funding, negative trailing FCF, and 2027 capex expected 50-70% above 2026.
Credit spread pressure from heavy hyperscaler debt supply, per JPM's Spear.
Mag7 acting as a source of funds.

tension_points.bull_case: Capex is surging while Street 2027 AWS growth sits about a point lower. Bulls see 2027 AWS growth of 45-50% versus the Street's +35%. AWS capacity is sold out and committed dollar growth is accelerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Everyone expects the beat-and-raise, so it is already priced. Positioning is crowded (8/10 Goldman, 9/10 UBS) and the tape punishes misses and gives clean beats little credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AWS growth below the roughly 42% buyside bogey or operating income below the $28B bogey would break the beat-and-raise case.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Sheridan says near-term risk looks overstated, AI-referred traffic is small, and Amazon keeps engagement within its ecosystem. UBS also calls the risk overblown.
tension_points.bear_case: Deutsche says agent-led shopping could reduce exposure to Sponsored Products, which slowed about 100bps in 3Q. Schilsky says punting on the question will not go over well.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A direct partnership with Meta or a clear agent strategy from management on the call would ease the bear case.

tension_points.bull_case: Deutsche says support continues if AWS keeps strong revenue and operating-income growth as capacity comes online, and partner-funded capacity and in-house silicon could moderate direct funding.
tension_points.bear_case: Trailing FCF is negative, 2027 capex is expected 50-70% above 2026, and funding has moved to bonds, sterling debt and SPVs. JPM sees credit spreads pressured into 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: AWS margins in the low 40s would supply the returns evidence the market now demands.
